body.p: Sands & Kenny's Commercial and General Melbourne Directory for 1858.
A copy of the full directory is held by Melbourne History Resources, and you can read it online.

The 1858 directory is too early to have a Carlton section. The streets that later became Carlton are listed under North Melbourne (pp. 187–191), alphabetically by name within each street rather than house by house. The listings here are the streets that lie in what later became Carlton: Bouverie, Cardigan, Drummond, Leicester, Lygon, Madeline (now Swanston), Rathdowne, and the eastern parts of Queensberry and Victoria streets, which the directory lists separately as Queensberry-street, East and Victoria-street, East. The 1858 listings give no side of the street, and only some give a house number.
